findings.text: Pressure file enablement is exposed as a global predicate with two build configurations, one consulting a disable branch plus a feature mask and one reporting unavailability. Callers use it to decide whether optional pressure entries accompany base entries.

Child state traversal is available to other core components and tolerates concurrent unlinking. It starts at the first child when no cursor is supplied and otherwise advances through sibling linkage, falling back to serial ordered search when the cursor has been released.

Statistics initialization is exposed for subsystem state creation and prepares per processor tracking. Root self entries reuse preallocated base storage, subsystems lacking a flush hook need no further work, and remaining cases allocate per processor state with self terminated update lists.

Grace period deferred work submission is provided for asynchronous cleanup. It claims pending ownership exactly once, records the target queue, requests hurried grace handling, and reports whether submission occurred.

Hierarchy root lifecycle helpers are exposed for setup and teardown. One initializes list linkage, group counts, flags, agent path, name and clone behavior, one frees a root through deferred reclamation, and one adjusts dynamic modification preference under thread group exclusion.

Legacy hierarchy filesystem behavior is defined by a syscall operation table covering renaming, option display, directory creation and removal, and path rendering. Mount handling selects or builds the backing root before those operations become usable.

Directory publication is idempotent and mode aware. Already visible states return success without further work, self states receive hierarchy specific base entries with optional pressure entries when enabled, and other states receive their subsystem collection. Visibility is only marked after full success.

Control file installation honors placement constraints that depend on hierarchy flavor, root versus descendant position, and debug mode. Files whose constraints do not match the target group are silently skipped during both addition and removal passes.

Control file names carry a subsystem prefix derived from current hierarchy flavor unless prefixing is disabled globally or for the entry. Debug entries receive an additional distinguishing marker, while unprefixed entries use the bare entry name.

Control file access rights are derived from handler presence. Any read handler yields broad readability, any write handler yields writability that is broad only when explicitly marked and otherwise owner restricted, and handlerless entries receive no access bits.

Subsystem visibility combines three considerations: direct enablement in the control set means visible, absence from the membership mask means hidden, and remaining cases are visible only in the unified hierarchy when the subsystem requests implicit presence.

A global group mutex serializes creation, publication, teardown and control changes. File table updates, identifier assignment, state linkage, online promotion, dying marking and reference teardown all require the holder to own this exclusion.

Finer grained protection complements the global mutex. Identifier tables use bottom half safe spinning with allocation preload, notification state uses interrupt safe spinning around pointer clearing plus synchronous timer cancellation, dynamic preference uses thread group write exclusion, and child walking accepts either global ownership or read side grace protection.

Subsystem state nodes form a parent child sibling tree anchored at their group and subsystem. Each node carries an identifier, serial order, lifecycle flags, shared and online reference tracking, descendant tally, statistics storage and deferred destruction work, with parent linkage and live group pinning established at creation.

Group objects aggregate identity, hierarchy position and control bookkeeping. Observed members include kernfs linkage, root pointer, self state, subsystem slots, control and membership masks with saved copies for rollback, domain pointer, descendant limits and tallies, dying counts per subsystem, process list synchronization, offline waiting and release work.

Subsystem state moves from allocation through linkage and publication to eventual teardown. After reference, identifier and statistics setup it joins the parent child list, becomes reachable through online promotion with ancestor accounting, gains directory presence when visible, then on removal is marked dying with directory teardown, has its shared reference killed with cross processor confirmation, and is freed through grace deferred work.

Control updates use a save attempt settle pattern over the affected subtree. On failure prior control, mask and domain values are restored and propagated, then a disable pass removes states that lost membership or clears directories that became invisible, invoking reset hooks where present.

Legacy mount root choice validates requested options, waits for previously dying subsystems by requesting a restart when a live reference cannot be taken, reuses an existing root whose name and subsystem set match, and otherwise allocates and initializes a fresh root only in the initial namespace before enabling it.

Partial directory expansion never remains half visible. Failure while adding a batch entry causes earlier entries from the same batch to be removed, and failure while populating subsystem collections causes earlier collections to be withdrawn, preserving an all or nothing appearance.

Iteration over children remains safe when entries are concurrently released. Released cursors are detected through a dedicated flag and resolved by scanning for the next higher serial number instead of following potentially stale linkage, relying on monotonic append order and serialized release.

Dying transition coordinates with concurrent population observers through ordering guarantees. Killed notification precedes dying marking, directory teardown precedes disassociation, ancestor tallies and dying counts are adjusted up the chain, and parent resources are retained until child destruction completes.

Lifecycle and placement behavior is governed by named flag families. One family tracks visibility, online presence, dying progress and release completion, another selects hierarchy specific placement and root only or non root only scope, and further bits control debug visibility, prefix suppression and broad writability.
